prompt: Stage 4-1, level 7, 38 gold, 48 HP after a bad stage 3, three losses in a row. Your friend says not to worry: 'you get an augment next round to fix the board'. Augments come at 2-1, 3-2 and 4-2. Is your friend right, and what does it mean for this round?

options.label: Yes: 4-2 is the third and last augment. This round, roll for 2-stars anyway; the augment is a bonus on top of the board, not a rescue
No: augments come at 2-1, 3-1 and 4-1, so you already missed this stage's pick
No: 4-2 is the carousel; the next augment is at 5-2

explanation:
Augments come three times a game: 2-1, 3-2 and 4-2. So yes, there is one next round, and it is the last one. But an augment is a bonus on top of the board, not a replacement for it: at 48 HP with three losses in a row the fights at 4-1 and 4-2 still happen, and stage-4 losses cost 10 HP or more each. The plan this round is the standard one for 4-1: you are level 7 already, so roll some of the 38 gold for 2-stars on your carry and tank, and pick the 4-2 augment that helps the board you will have then (a combat augment, not an econ one at this HP).

The wrong answers are wrong about the calendar. 4-1 is a fight, 4-4 is the carousel and 4-7 is monsters; the only augment round in stage 4 is 4-2. Knowing where the augment sits stops you from banking gold for a rescue that is not coming and from missing the one that is.
principle: Augments come at 2-1, 3-2 and 4-2. They add to a board; they do not replace fixing it.
commonMistake: Holding gold at 4-1 waiting for the augment to 'fix' a losing board, and arriving at 4-3 with the same board and less HP.
hint: Write down the three augment rounds and check which of them is still ahead of you. Then ask whether an augment stops the next loss by itself.
